    Pearl (PRL): the multiply is real, the bid is not

    Updated deep dive on Pearl, the matrix-multiplication proof-of-work chain: first-principles unit economics, on-chain holders and pools, emissions, liquidity, and bear/base/bull scenarios at Oct 4 prices. Research only.

    Research only. Not financial advice. All times are ET (UTC-4). Labeling rule for this note: every hashrate, supply and market cap figure is marked unconfirmed. Each still carries its source, but none of them has been independently confirmed. Hashrate is an explorer estimate derived from difficulty. Supply comes from an explorer and an aggregator, cross-checked against the emission formula. Market cap is an aggregator figure on thin venues. Charts: market and peer charts use CoinGecko only. On-chain charts use pearlchain.live. Explainer diagrams are simplified schematics. Each caption names its source and fetch time (ET).

    Price line (refreshed): PRL $1.052 on CoinGecko (coins/pearl-2, last_updated 2026-10-04 15:22:40 ET), 24h change +0.10%, 7d -35.3%, 30d +192%, 24h volume $2.09M. Market cap $351.5M (CoinGecko, unconfirmed). Fully diluted value about $2.21B at the 2.1B max supply (derived, unconfirmed). Circulating supply field 334,497,944. Rank 137.

    The call in one paragraph

    Pearl is still the most serious proof-of-useful-work design we have reviewed, and the team is unusually credible. The token is a different question. Spot is $1.052, down about 5% from the Oct 2 note's $1.11 print, with volume about half that earlier tape. On-chain usage is holding up better than price. Fees since launch are about 7,214 PRL (about $7,600). Issuance at the 194 second target is about $1.07M a day, 51% of the same-timestamp volume. FP8 / Pearl-GEMM is an open pull request, not consensus. Our research view at about $1.052 is avoid an outright long (medium conviction). Not a high-conviction short: the book is thin, and the bull tail (FP8 live plus a deeper venue) is real. Probability-weighted geometric midpoints are about $0.89 at 3 months and $0.77 at 12 months, both below spot.

    What Pearl is

    Pearl is a proof-of-work Layer 1 derived from Bitcoin. Mainnet launched 2026-04-27. It replaces SHA-256 with noised matrix multiplication, so GPU work that serves AI inference can mine PRL at the same time. Pearl calls this "duplex compute". The core construction is in arXiv 2504.09971. Max supply is 2.1B PRL, with a smooth emission curve that puts half the supply out by block 650,226. The explorer reports a 194 second target and a current block reward of 2,282.69 PRL (pearlchain.live stats, 15:24 ET).

    • Team: Omri Weinstein, Ilan Komargodski, Idan Sugerman. Rafael Pass is research scientist and advisor (economics paper arXiv 2606.06700). Fair-launch claims (no premine, no VC allocation) appear in secondary writeups; we did not audit genesis.
    • Code: GitHub pearl-research-labs/pearl, created 2026-04-19, active on Oct 4 (335 stars, 81 forks, 92 open issues, fetched 15:27 ET). Node version on the explorer tip is pearld 1.4.8. FP8 pull request #311 was still open (updated 2026-10-04 07:29 ET).
    • Partner: Together AI's May 15 blog announced an "exclusive partnership" and said the Gemma-4-31B-it-Pearl endpoint "is discounted by over 25%, offset by the future value of crypto emissions" (page saved 15:27 ET). The same-day model page says the model is not on Together's Serverless API. Terms of the offset are not published.
    • Pearl's own inference product at pearlresearch.ai is priced in USD, not PRL. Today there is no clear token sink.

    First principles: what the scarce unit pays

    The scarce unit is a winning noised matrix multiply, paid in new PRL. Fees are not the metric.

    • At the 194 second target: about 445 blocks a day and 1,016,620 PRL a day, about $1,069,484 at $1.052. Explorer hashrate 48.18 EH/s (difficulty-derived, unconfirmed), so about $22,200 per EH/s per day. All-time fees 7,214 PRL, about $7,589 (0.002% of formula supply). [pearlchain.live stats 15:24 ET; CoinGecko 15:22 ET]
    • Whitepaper (September 2026): each tile of the product "doubles as a lottery ticket for block production." That describes the FP8 spec. Mainnet is still INT-8. Weinstein (Sep 25): the live protocol "is INT-8 only, and adds 10-15% overhead," with Pearl-GEMM "expected to launch within weeks," and spam mining "will always" be allowed.
    • Unit economics, one GPU-hour that could mine or be rented (ASSUMPTION scale from Basu's June 24 EH/s / 320,000 GPU / 112 MW census to 48.18 EH/s): new PRL about 7 cents per GPU-hour; May 31 vast.ai RTX 3090 median rental $0.34 (stale); protocol fee about $0.000003 per GPU-hour. Power cash cost per PRL about $0.13 to $0.76 (base $0.32 at $0.06/kWh). Rental cost per PRL about $1.94 to $6.19 across that band. Issuance is revenue to miners and dilution to holders. It is not protocol revenue.
    • Reconciliation: Oct 1/2/3 explorer coins 1,065,348 / 897,103 / 994,445 (three-day average 985,632) versus target 1,016,620, gap about -3.1%, inside a 15% band.

    On-chain picture

    Sources: pearlchain.live keyless API, fetched 2026-10-04 15:24 to 15:29 ET (stats, charts, addresses, pools, and a crawl of blocks 123001 to 123200).

    • Hashrate used in this note: 48.18 EH/s (unconfirmed), difficulty-derived over a 21,600 second window, "not measured computation."
    • Supply: formula supply at height 123,200 is 334,511,640 PRL (15.93% minted). CoinGecko circulating field 334,497,944 (0.004% gap). Explorer address total 345,015,315 (about 3.1% higher). Holder shares use the address total and say so.
    • Issuance: target about 1.02M PRL/day. At $1.052 that is about $1.07M, 51% of the $2.09M same-timestamp volume. Annualized mint is about 111% of formula supply.
    • Dilution path (formula at 194 s pace from height 123,200): about 422.4M PRL in 91 days (+26%) implies about $0.83 at a flat $351.5M cap; about 641.1M in 365 days (+92%) implies about $0.55. Using the recent 186 s average block time instead moves the 12-month supply only to about 652M / $0.54. The call does not depend on that choice.
    • Holder concentration: top 10 addresses 15.5%, top 100 44.0%, top 1,000 75.9%. Forty-two whale-tier addresses hold 33.8%. 117,195 addresses. No exchange, team, or treasury label is in the saved pages.
    • Launch week: 125.1M PRL mined Apr 27 to May 3 (UTC), 37.4% of today's formula supply. Not a premine. Still a concentration fact.
    • Pool concentration: explorer 24h window (864 blocks): Kryptex 52.3%, PearlHash 27.8%, top 3 about 85.7%. Our coinbase crawl of 200 tip blocks: one payee 50.0%, top 3 86.5%, nine payees. Both cuts say one operator is near half.
    • Activity: monthly average daily transactions: June 21,519, August 8,792, September 15,479, October (first 4 days) 10,330. Average daily active addresses: June 25,037, August 11,327, September 16,899, October 18,988. October usage is holding up better than price. A large share of transactions are still coinbase and pool payouts.

    Attention and use (no social counts)

    Attention series from X and Google Trends stay off this public note. What we can say from price and usage alone:

    • Price peaked later than the spring usage peak. Daily-series high remains the Sep 28 00:00 UTC point at $1.534 (about 31% above spot). Intraday ATH $1.76 is about 40% above spot.
    • Since the Oct 2 note: spot from about $1.11 to $1.052; CoinGecko 24h volume from about $4.8M to about $2.1M. October active addresses (four-day average about 19k) sit above the September average. Usage is not the thing that broke. The bid did.
    • Claims check (re-fetched Oct 4): Together discount wording verified in the blog; serverless availability denied on the later model page. "3% to 5% overhead" as a description of mainnet is false (Weinstein: 10-15% live). "Mining is paid AI" is not shown in Basu's June software census. Unverified social hashrate and listing-amount claims are not inputs here.

    Analogies and layered TAM

    Useful-work stories have a base rate. Primecoin (CoinGecko, last_updated 2026-09-28) prints about $0.034 versus an ATH of $7.27 on 2013-11-29, down about 99.5%. Bitcoin is only a partial analogy: deep books, 17 years, and work that is not sold as useful. Pearl is 160 days old, two thin venues, about 16% of supply out, and about 92% more supply in a year at the formula.

    Built from units times price (no team TAM figure was on the saved primary pages):

    • Core (in the chain): all-time fee average about $47/day, about $17k/year. Probability that core fees are material in 12 months: about 8%.
    • Adjacent (partner discount): Together discount funded by emissions is not cash to holders. Probability of a second named production partner in 12 months: about 20%.
    • Option (aspirational): if 10% of a scaled fleet ran paid work at the May $0.34 rental proxy, about $190M/year (ASSUMPTION, unproven). Probability material in 12 months: about 10%. Earliest plausible year looks like 2027 if FP8 merges and demand shows up.

    Catalysts and risks

    Catalysts:

    1. FP8 / Pearl-GEMM hardfork. Still "within weeks" as of Sep 25, with no date. Main fundamental catalyst. PR 311 open on Oct 4.
    2. A second named duplex partner, or Together's endpoint becoming clearly live on serverless.
    3. A venue with real depth (or a confirmed tier-1 listing). None in the Oct 4 ticker pull.
    4. Attestable proof that a material share of hashrate does paid inference. Fees above 1% of block rewards for 30 days would be an early sign.

    Risks:

    • Dilution: +26% supply in 3 months and +92% in 12 (unconfirmed supply path).
    • Thin, low-trust venues; issuance already half of reported volume.
    • Pool concentration near 50%.
    • Launch-week supply concentration.
    • Rentable, merge-mined hashrate, and two consensus incidents already (July MoE disable; August salted noise-seed hardfork).
    • Ticker collisions.
    • Upgradeable-bridge claim carried, not re-verified.

    What has to be true (and what would change the view)

    Starting from $1.052 and $351.5M. At a 25x fee multiple (ASSUMPTION, range 15x to 40x), the cap implies about $39k/day of fees. Today's all-time average is about $47/day. Gap about 800x.

    Bullish falsifiers:

    • FP8 live on mainnet (node version moves after PR 311 merges) with measured end-to-end overhead of 3% or less, and within about 60 days attestable data showing over 30% of hashrate doing paid inference.
    • Fees above 1% of block rewards over 30 days.
    • A venue with cost-to-move-up above about $250k, or a confirmed tier-1 ticker.
    • Spot holding above $1.80 for five daily CoinGecko closes after such a venue appears.

    Bearish confirmations:

    • FP8 still open on 2026-12-31.
    • A single payee above 60% over 1,000 blocks.
    • Top-10 balances down 20% in a week with price under $0.65 on labeled exchange-bound flow (we cannot label that flow today).

    Scenarios (research only, subjective probabilities)

    These scenarios use supply of about 422M at 3 months and about 641M at 12 months (unconfirmed).

    • 3 months, bear (45%): $0.30 to $0.65. FP8 slips, miners sell into a thinner book, price moves toward the power-cost band.
    • 3 months, base (40%): $0.70 to $1.25. FP8 is announced but not decisive. Market cap grows slower than supply.
    • 3 months, bull (15%): $1.60 to $2.80. FP8 on mainnet and a deeper venue. Not a fee sink yet.
    • 12 months, bear (50%): $0.12 to $0.40. Usefulness stays unproven. Supply up about 92%. Attention stays cold.
    • 12 months, base (35%): $0.45 to $1.00. Some duplex use. Dilution wins.
    • 12 months, bull (15%): $1.80 to $4.50. Fees become visible and a real venue exists.

    Geometric midpoints of the ranges: 3 months $0.44 / $0.94 / $2.12; 12 months $0.22 / $0.67 / $2.85. Arithmetic weight of those midpoints: about $0.89 and $0.77. Log-weighted figures (not the headline method shared with the Oct 2 note): $0.75 and $0.48. All sit below spot. That shape is why the research view is to avoid a long rather than to take a high-conviction short.
